limitations: The reviewer is a separate reviewer agent session on the same host and the same account, launched by the producer session. It is not a second machine and not a human. The reviewer is a Claude agent session (model Sonnet 5.5, claude-sonnet-5-5) and reviews a row that the Claude Code CLI with a Sonnet model produced; the previous review of this row used an Opus session. The duplicate rule, the restatement rule and the digest rule were written on 2026-10-05, after the captures of 2026-09-15 and after earlier approvals.

This is a delta review of a blanking-only change. Set v9 differs from the previously approved set v8 only by blanked strings, digests that follow from them, the transformation receipt, and the manifest. The semantic review of the scores (duplicate safety, density, usage, model, reconciliation and file-change rules, the Read case) is the previous review (claude-cli-independent-public-review-v5, reviewer opus-independent-reviewer-claude-cli); this reviewer re-ran the replays and found all 31 metric rows of each run equal to v8, and did not re-derive the semantics.

Vendor instruction text was blanked at equal byte length: in each transcript, every string of an attachment record except its type and the platform of an environment attachment, 155 strings and 66,326 raw JSON characters per run (the producer reports 65,547 decoded characters). Keys of the blanked JSON objects (for example the parameter names of tool schemas) and every non-attachment record stay. The reviewer found no vendor instruction phrase of the private parent in any public file. The kept value darwin is an operating-system name, not vendor text; the public inputs builder reads the OS from it. Thinking signatures (opaque base64) and the capture working directory names remain.
Capture provenance is archived and was not re-acquired. The reviewer ran no harness and did not read the personal session store.

The packets are sanitized derivatives of private packets. The account e-mail and the home user name are replaced by equal-length aliases; the home alias keeps the length of the home name (5 characters). The reviewer compared the packets with the private parent inside the repository only.

This approval covers the three packets and the public bundle only. summary.json and the three *-private-transformation.json files beside the packets hold a private parent manifest pin and hashes of private originals; with them a guessed e-mail or home user name is confirmed. They must not be published. The candidate directories v4 to v8 and the review directories v2 to v5 hold private digests or unblanked vendor text and must not be published either.

The previous reviews found two digest defects in earlier sets (v5 and v7). In v8 and v9 the digests of capture-time files that hold private digests (evidence_31, broad_wrapper, helper_ledger, turn1 and turn2 stdout, decoder source in inputs/attempt.json) are zeroed. The reviewer's tests (producer digest check; e-mail and home name restored into every public file and hashed whole, by line and by JSON value; digests of all files of the private parent v7 and of set v8) reach no public field of the three packets, the bundle or the receipts. A digest of a document that the reviewer could not see cannot be excluded by test.

The six root inventory metadata_digest values per packet stay public on the sanitizer allowlist. Each is a digest over inode ids, sizes and nanosecond times of about 4100 files of the personal Claude projects root. The reviewer accepts the reason: the preimage is not in any public or capture-time file and cannot be rebuilt from a guessed name.

Duplicate safety is 13 of 19: 16 events; both prompts are stated twice (queue-operation enqueue and user record) and the Edit call is stated twice (tool_use block and toolUseResult of its result record). The Read result holds the only argument of the Read call (the file path) and is not counted, by the rubric sentence that a call whose only arguments name its target is restated only by a record that also holds the tool name. That sentence was written after the previous reviewer raised the case. The literal all-arguments reading gives 12 of 20 and about 0.25 points less per run.

The usage, model, reconciliation and file-change rules were amended on 2026-10-03 and 2026-10-04, after these runs were captured on 2026-09-15. The amendments move four metrics (16 points) to measured for this configuration.

The observer reports cache_read 0 in 6 of 6 turns while the native sum is 47165 to 55750 tokens per turn. The packet cannot explain the observer value because the stdout stream is not retained. Input, output and cache-creation sums agree exactly.

The comparator accepts a turn-level usage join without a value check, the Claude projection has a model-unreported fallback, and the edit-hash helper does not bind the result filePath or check a multi-edit chain. None of these paths is triggered in these packets: each has one Edit of fixture_project/checkout.py and usage on the final-answer record.

The packets keep operator-machine metadata (file and project-key counts of the personal Claude projects root, inode ids, timestamps, OS and shell version in the root inventory), Anthropic request and message ids, and stale capture-time fields in inputs/attempt.json.

The packet runtime equals the review snapshot (commit 20d71d7) except the two package __init__ stubs. portable.complete_root relies on a later-qualified manifest that the reviewer did not re-verify. Non-broad metric locators bind the whole session artifact, not single lines. The inputs/root-evidence folders hold no copy of another run's transcript, only manifests, inventories and decode documents; they hold no vendor text.
